title: Transactional method calling another transactional method
short: Propagation applies when the call crosses the Spring proxy boundary.
answer: REQUIRED usually shares; REQUIRES_NEW suspends the outer transaction. Self-invocation can bypass interception.
interview: Propagation applies when the call crosses the Spring proxy boundary.

title: Transactional exception vs global handler
short: The transaction interceptor decides rollback; controller advice formats the HTTP response.
answer: A RuntimeException propagating through the transactional proxy can trigger rollback. Advice is not the rollback mechanism.
interview: The transaction interceptor decides rollback; controller advice formats the HTTP response.

title: How does Spring Boot auto-configuration work?

answer: It relies on conditional configuration classes registered in \META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports\ (previously \spring.factories\). title: Propagation types in `@Transactional`.
short: \REQUIRED\ (default) joins an existing transaction or creates one if none exists. \REQUIRES\_NEW\ always suspends any existing transaction and starts a fresh one. \SUPPORTS\ joins one if present, else runs non-transactionally. \MANDATORY\ r
answer: \REQUIRED\ (default) joins an existing transaction or creates one if none exists. \REQUIRES\_NEW\ always suspends any existing transaction and starts a fresh one. \SUPPORTS\ joins one if present, else runs non-transactionally. \MANDATORY\ requires an existing transaction, throwing if none exists. \NEVER\/\NOT\_SUPPORTED\ run without a transaction, the former erroring if one exists. \NESTED\ creates a savepoint within the current transaction that can be rolled back independently.

title: Explain the complete request lifecycle in Spring Boot.
short: Request arrives at the embedded server → passes through the servlet filter chain (e.g. Spring Security filters, CORS, logging) → \DispatcherServlet\ resolves the matching handler via \HandlerMapping\ → any \HandlerInterceptor\s run pre-hand
answer: Request arrives at the embedded server → passes through the servlet filter chain (e.g. Spring Security filters, CORS, logging) → \DispatcherServlet\ resolves the matching handler via \HandlerMapping\ → any \HandlerInterceptor\s run pre-handle → the controller method executes (with argument resolution and validation) → the return value is converted to the response body via message converters → interceptors run post-handle → the response is sent, with any exceptions along the way routed to an \@ExceptionHandler\.
